title: Handoff kind
description: A kind of artefact a task produces or consumes. Keys are `handoff` spec §8's; the four content types are §3.2's and the four scope tags are §4's.

name.description: The kind name. Unique; this is what `Handoff.type` holds.

description.description: What this kind of artefact is, for a human.

content_type.description: One of the four in `handoff` spec §3.2. The type fixes what `items` must carry and what the README's sections are. `reproducible` is the richest: a thing that ran, the way to run it again, what came out, and what to watch for.

scope.description: A closed vocabulary, and a handoff carries exactly one (`handoff` spec §4). It decides storage, permission, and retention together. An `addons` handoff cannot satisfy a `fixed.required` input — §4.2.

items_schema.description: The declared keys of `items` and their shapes; runtime-generated keys are permitted where this says so. Typed loosely ON PURPOSE. Whether it is a valid schema is a named load-time check calling `Draft202012Validator.check_schema`, not a `$ref` to the metaschema: `docs/design.md` §3.5 measured the `$ref` form producing eight identical unactionable errors for one mistake.

readme_sections.description: Sections the README must carry, beyond the content type's defaults.

validators.description: Validator spec names. **At least one**, unless the escape-hatch flag is set — and that is a load-time check rather than `minItems`, because the flag is a run-time argument the schema cannot see, and a kind it lets through must be admitted AND reported (`handoff` spec §5.3).

dependencies.description: What a consumer's machine must satisfy: hardware, software, a container image. Deliberately not further constrained — `handoff` spec §7 says the `env` item carries this for a `reproducible` kind and that for the others 'the kind's schema declares what applies', so fixing a shape here would be inventing a requirement.
